state.product: Miu World: online Minecraft-like 3D voxel learning game for all ages (children and adults), web today on phones/iPads, mobile app later. North star from the owner: lively, never boring. Quests teach Vietnamese grade-2 textbook content.
state.owner_request: The owner looked at the boss fight on a phone and said: the boss fight should be interactive play instead of feeling like doing a main quest step. The owner told the team to let Jev choose the direction and then build it.
current_boss_fight: A modal over the paused 3D world, same frame as every other quest challenge: banner title, HP bar (e.g. 400/500), a 2D emoji/illustration avatar with a speech bubble and progress dots, a text multiple-choice question card with 3 answer buttons, and a support panel (Guide, Hint after 1 wrong, Answer after 2 wrong, 'Solve (-100 HP)').

Data: each boss has maxHp and 4-6 turns; each turn is a multiple-choice question with server-side right/wrong feedback lines and support layers. 12 big bosses and 42 zone guardians (about 260 questions) already written.
The server judges answers, HP and rewards; the client must not decide rewards. A co-op team-boss mode shares HP across up to 4 players taking turns.
The 3D boss is not shown during the fight; there is no attack, hit or dodge animation.
A separate minigame framework exists (15+ real-time Canvas 2D games with taps/swipes, e.g. paper-io, unblock-ferry) but it is not used for bosses.
constraints: Keep the learning content and the server as source of truth for right/wrong, HP and rewards; reuse the 260 written questions without rewriting them.
Keep the support layers and the 'copy the question and answer into the notebook after each right answer' feature (the owner's top outcome).
Young children must be able to read calmly: no losing because a timer ran out; adults should still find it fun.
Touch-first: must work on a phone in portrait and on iPad.
Content must stay varied, never repetitive.
Must keep within the 3D draw-call budget on iPad.

direction.instructions: Which direction should the boss fight redesign take so it feels like interactive play rather than a quest step, given the constraints?

criteria.live-3d-duel: Keep the 3D world running with the real boss model facing the child; the camera frames both, the question becomes a compact card at the bottom. A right answer plays the child's attack (projectile, hit flash, boss staggers, HP bar drains with numbers); a wrong answer plays the boss's harmless counter (child dodges, light shake); the boss has idle/taunt/defeat animations. Answering is still tapping a choice. Turn-based, no timer.
criteria.action-minigame: Turn each boss into a real-time arcade minigame on the existing Canvas 2D framework: the boss throws answer bubbles or obstacles, the child dodges and catches or shoots the right answer before it disappears; HP drains on hits. The 3D world stays paused behind it.
criteria.hybrid-duel-with-play-moves: Live 3D duel as above, plus each turn the child answers through a varied, gentle play move instead of a plain button: aim and fling a charm at the shield bearing the right answer, tap the right answer orb as it floats around the boss, drag a power gem onto the right answer, or charge a combo by tapping. Moves rotate between turns and between bosses for variety; no timer, wrong picks bounce off harmlessly; the server still judges each pick.
